free.title: JUST OPENED - House of Kong
free.caption:
JUST OPENED · GORILLAZ HOUSE OF KONG

Gorillaz just opened their first NYC pop-up, and it's not in Manhattan, it's tucked inside the Brooklyn Navy Yard.

House of Kong turns the Agger Fish Building into a walk-through of the band's 25-year history: listening rooms, tour artifacts, and a giant Mountain on the way to the gift shop. It's self-paced, takes about an hour, and this is the exhibit's only stop on the East Coast.

Book ahead, timed entry has been selling out on weekends.

Running through September 28. Save this before it's gone.

📸 Gorillaz

food.title: FOOD - Herbie's Burgers
food.caption:
FOOD · HERBIE'S BURGERS

Herbie's Burgers just opened its second New York location, and this one's on 1st Avenue in the East Village.

The Albany import made its NYC debut in Williamsburg earlier this year, now there's a smash burger and a shake a few blocks from Tompkins Square Park. The lineup runs from a $3 slider to the $18.25 Herbfather, plus a vegan double that holds its own, shoestring fries, and glass-bottle Mexican Coke.

The kitchen stays open until 2AM most nights, so this doubles as a late-night option.

Bookmark it for your next East Village crawl.

📸 Herbie's Burgers

art.title: ART - Mercer Labs
art.caption:
ART · MERCER LABS

Mercer Labs in Lower Manhattan is 15 rooms of interactive art and tech with no guide and no script, you just wander.

Wave your hand to conduct a robotic cellist in the Freedom Room, watch a robotic arm draw in sand, or stand inside a hologram built from 500,000 suspended points of light. It's self-directed, most visits run 60-90 minutes, and yes, there's a ball pit.

Thursday through Sunday it stays open until 10PM, so it doubles as an after-work stop.

Save this for your next indoor day in the city.

📸 Mercer Labs
